items.name: all_lines
items.direction: Narrate for a premium documentary YouTube channel about money and history. The narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. These are separate short lines for YouTube Shorts: read each one as its own complete take, with the same voice, energy and loudness every time, and leave a clear one-second pause between lines. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers; questions end with a curious lift.
lines: Narrator
Your $100 bill used to buy almost 5 ounces of gold. Now it buys a fortieth. What broke?
Narrator
So what replaced gold in your wallet? The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
Before coins, you could lose a whole day trading chickens for one goat. Why did gold end up as money?
Narrator
Then gold got too heavy to carry. The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
1,000 years ago, your savings in China cost you a backpack of iron. So why did paper win, and what broke?
Narrator
Then Europe chained paper to gold. The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
You could risk 10 years in prison for keeping gold in 1933. But why?
Narrator
So what did 1971 do to your dollar? The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
Your dollar's gold promise started cracking in 1965. Why did France want 300 million dollars in gold?
Narrator
Three years later, Nixon shut the gold window. The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
Your money lost its last link to gold on August 15th, 1971. What happened that Sunday?
Narrator
So why does the world still run on dollars? The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
Why do you still pay in dollars, 50 years after gold left? Blame your family group chat.
Narrator
But central banks are quietly buying gold again. The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
Narrator
Why can't you just go back to gold? All 222,600 tonnes would cost you more than you think.
Narrator
So what actually backs your money today? The full story's on Money Mirage. Follow for more.
